html:
Castanor (B32)

Region in the English rating survey: Escann.

In one sentence: Earn the right to undertake the Trials amid Escann's ruins, then revive an ancient empire gone for more than four centuries. Legions, old cities and Dominions provide its strength; human-centred expulsion policies are the cost behind its restoration.

Story: extremely high | Mission-tree length: exceptionally long (156 direct B32 mission definitions; the file also contains 15 B61 The Edhardrachon civil-war missions, not B32 missions) | Mission-tree currency: the local file was modified on 2026-09-07 and supports EU4 v1.37.5.0; file time is not a confirmed rework date | Distinctiveness: extremely high | Tedium: high (formation qualification, Trials, construction and late conquest) | Early pressure: high, chiefly before formation | Expansion capacity: extremely high.

An ancient imperial legacy, not a 1444 starting country

[Local localisation] Castanor (B32) is the country displayed as 卡斯塔诺 in the current Chinese localisation. No directly selectable B32 empire occupies the 1444 map. Its country-history template's ruler dated 474 and designated capital do not establish continuing land ownership in 1444. First play an adventurer or regional state's Escanni prologue and qualify for restoration. Castellyr, Adenica and others can therefore provide routes, but none is Castanor's sole designated predecessor. Black Castanor is another path explicitly excluded by the decision.

[Wiki] The offline English Wiki uses Castanor for several historical incarnations of Castan's Empire. Castan the Progenitor founded the early state after leading the Castanite Exodus; later emperors expanded throughout Cannor and ushered in a broader golden age. After the Day of Ashen Skies, central order weakened over a long period and local lords contested the throne. The united empire finally dissolved after the War of the Sorcerer-King. Knightly kingdoms and Castanor's legacy then survived in Escann until the Greentide destroyed the old order. Mission flavour likewise treats Castonath, ancient walls, old dynasties and the Dragonwake as memories the restorer must confront. Neither ancient victories nor future missions establish territory already held in 1444. Parts of the dedicated late-imperial Wiki page remain empty outlines; this article does not invent their missing details.

Qualifying for restoration: win Escann, then face the Trials

[Local script] Eligible entries include reformed Escanni adventurers and countries that have formed Adenica, Blademarches, Castellyr, Farraneán or Corintar, with an additional entry for Marrhold (B36). Occupying the capital with just any country is not enough. Unlock the Castanor option after the Escanni wars; own and core all of Castonath; hold province 840, the North Citadel, with its Castanorian Citadel; retain the Castonath Patricians estate and Human Administration modifier; and be at peace with an allowed independent status. A ruler who has already attempted the Trials during their lifetime cannot immediately retry. The difficulty of the predecessor campaign depends on the country chosen: no single player route is the only solution.

The crucial technical distinction is that for a player, the decision starts the Trials rather than immediately changing to B32. Only the success event changes Tag, adopts Castanorian culture, moves the capital to the North Citadel, raises government rank, switches to B32 missions and grants claims across Escanni regions. Who deserves to become the next Castan is therefore an actual mechanism, not just a cutscene. Official Dev Diary #25 presented the Trials, old cities, Legions and cultural projects as core design pillars. Its 2021 formation figures and event counts describe that design period; current gates follow the local decisions and events.

Legions, ancient cities and Dominions

After formation, the tree is more than a demand to paint the map. Rebuild Legions and Legion roads, reconnecting citadels, the White Walls, Dragonforges and other ancient works to the imperial system. The Castonath Patricians supply commercial and administrative resources but also constitute a political force to accommodate. As the empire advances, Dominions and subjects govern its frontiers, while Castanorian culture and human political identity become common standards for integrating different regions. Workshops, industry, artificery and distant ruins appear later. Restoration is thus not merely a chain of wars, but a construction project that turns ancient legacies into a new empire.

The scale requires careful counting. The local structured library identifies 156 direct B32 missions, including later succession-war missions and regional branches that change with circumstances. The file's final 15 missions belong to the B61 The Edhardrachon civil-war opponent. They are not additional rewards that B32 receives sequentially beyond its 156, nor does every campaign display the same layout. Western-steppe paths vary with the actual situation of centaurs, the Lake Federation and other powers. Late succession war and local administration turn unifying an empire into the problem of keeping it together. [Community opinion] A 2022 long-campaign account questioned whether the tree could be completed before 1821. That is an older-version player's experience, not a current hard deadline or optimal route.

Restoration's human cost and recommendations

The v2.1 coordinates are expansion 99/100 | autocracy 88/100 | magic–artifice direction 35/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 58/100) | pluralism 15/100. Phase profiles run from rebuilding Castonath and the Legions (expansion 78, magic/artifice intensity 38) to restoring the ancient empire across Cannor (expansion 99, intensity 64). This territorial empire advances through monarchy, Legions and Dominions. The Trials, ancient engineering and artificery are present, but less central than warfare and state reconstruction. Cultural unification is not automatically evil, yet this tree goes beyond symbolic assimilation.

Its v2.1 values classification is Evil (24/100), with a declining trajectory. Phase values move from early imperial establishment and public construction (Neutral, 50/100) to cross-regional expulsions of goblins and gnolls (Evil, 20/100). These scores do not judge ancient empire, warfare or monarchy in themselves. The mission known in the Chinese text as reclaiming the homeland—currently titled “Exile the Exodus Goblins” in English—forces religion and culture changes in goblin-majority provinces in Bahar, Ourdia and other regions, adds 50 devastation, removes goblin minorities and awards money for the expelled population. The hillthrone mission, currently titled “Last Beastly Vestiges” in English, applies similar treatment to gnolls and lowers tolerance. Current scripts and localisation support actual population expulsion, not an abstract claim of cultural fusion. Anti-slavery language, dwarf–human cooperation, agriculture and public works also provide positive evidence, but cannot erase institutional expulsions across regions. Whether a gentler player branch exists, and the full in-game triggering details, remain unresolved.

Recommended for players who enjoy a long Escanni prologue, ancient imperial archaeology, Legion warfare, the Trials and an exceptionally long construction–conquest campaign. Avoid it if you want to select B32 directly in 1444, refuse to meet qualification and trial gates, dislike extensive late construction requirements, or do not want explicit population-expulsion narratives. See the original evidence page for sources, formation boundaries and counting conventions.

National Ideas

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as points are invested, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed: racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. A successor idea set does not automatically stack with the earlier set. Idea descriptions may recall history or express future aspirations; they do not automatically establish events already completed in 1444. Names and complete descriptions use the current Mod’s English localisation. Alternative and predecessor/successor sets remain separately conditional, including whether new ideas are accepted on formation.

Effect display units inherited from the source data are reproduced for parity, not revalidated here. Suspicious percentages and script-valued effects require separate review; raw values are shown below.

Castanor (B32) — Castanorian Ideas

Set ID: B32_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        OR = {
            tag = B32
            tag = B61
        }
    }

Castanorian Traditions

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

  • Prestige decay: -1.5% (prestige_decay; raw value -0.015).

1. The Battle of the Burning Hill

'Men of Castanor, how can your courage fail you today when the Castanites who founded this Empire walked ten thousand miles to flee slavery and chaos in Bulwar? How can your boldness fail you when two thousands years ago, led by Castan the Progenitor, they chose to fight and die with honour rather than to wait and die by the gnollish demonflame creeping up their fortified hill? To charge downhill, through fire and flame, and to clash with a foe that outnumbered you ten to one, was to be the last act of bravery... but Castellos saw otherwise. And during the Castanite charge, what did Castellos do? He appeared in the form of a Silver Dragon and blew the demonflame back at the gnolls, decisively altering the fate of mankind!

'Men of Castanor, be bold, for your arms will not fail you! Men of Castanor, hold your swords high, for we charge in the name of Castan and the Battle of the Burning Hill! And let our battlecry be heard by the gods, for they will answer with victory!'

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

2. The Great Restoration

Damenath, Vertesk, Bal Mire, Bal Ouord... The old Castanorian name of those cities and fortresses still today show the extent of the Greater Castan's Empire of the past. We will never forget that Castanor was the first human empire to rule these lands, and it is our sovereign, no, holy duty to take them back into the fold - for only when we rule all of Cannor can the lands be safe.

  • Core-creation cost: -10% (core_creation; raw value -0.1).

  • Governing Capacity Modifier: +15% (governing_capacity_modifier; raw value 0.15).

3. Castonath is Escann, and Escann is Castonath

Unlike all other cities in Cannor, Castonath was modelled after the dwarven holds of the Serpentspine. And like the greatest dwarven holds, it seems like rather than a city, an entire country was concentrated inside huge walls. All peoples of Escann is represented here, and no merchant can transport goods across Escann without making a stop at the sprawling markets of the City of Stone. For to trade with Escann is to trade with Castonath.

  • Caravan power: +25% (caravan_power; raw value 0.25).

4. Balgar's Wonders

Castanor's early successes at establishing itself as a great, lasting power was largely due to one dwarf: Balgar the Builder. His unparalleled mastery of architecture allowed for the construction for great works unseen in Cannor, from the legendary Dragonforge that armed the Castanorian Legions, to the White Walls that protected the fledgling empire from monstrous threats, to the famous citadels now scattered across Cannor.

  • Fort defense: +20% (defensiveness; raw value 0.2).

  • Fort maintenance: -10% (fort_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.1).

5. Revive the Castanorian Legions

The Castanorian Legions was the source of Castanor's power, and once marched across Cannor, Bulwar and the Salahad to ensure the empire's power. While the days of antiquity are long gone, we can reform our army structure to follow the old ways, and create an army truly fit for an empire.

  • Land force limit modifier: +20% (land_forcelimit_modifier; raw value 0.2).

  • global_regiment_cost: -5% (global_regiment_cost; raw value -0.05).

6. The Silver Dragon of Castanor

'Zaamalot the Black flew under the cover of night, burning Castonath to ash. All I could see were corpses and houses set ablaze, and in the flickers of flame I saw that even the white stone of the city had turned black under the Black Dragon's fiery breath. And then came down the sky what looked like a lighting, followed by a deafening but oddly musical roar of thunder. The Silver Dragon of Castanor, the legendary Avatar of Castellos, who helped Castan I at Burning Hill, was coming to our help again - and began to fight with Zaamalot.

'I knelt before the glistening silhouette instinctively, amazed at the creature's might and beauty. For once, the sight of dragonfire filled me with hope, and the flames reflected on his scales, shining so brightly that it seemed dawn had come for a moment. Two years after the end of the Dragonwake, I still feel blessed by this memory. All of our people should feel blessed that twice in history, Castellos himself appeared in the form of the Silver Dragon to save Castanor from a horrible end.'

-Autobiography of Castan XXXVII the Rebuilder

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

  • Stability cost modifier: -20% (stability_cost_modifier; raw value -0.2).

7. The Crown of Humanity

It truly is a pity that of all the artifacts recovered by the adventurers after the Greentide, the old silver crown of Castanor is still missing. Hence, when Castanor was rebuilt from its ashes, it was clear to all that the new Castan lacked a fitting crown. From today on, this will not be the case.

Out of silver and mithril, in one year of work, our best smiths forged a huge majestic crown. At the base, shining brightly, is a circlet sculpted to depict the White Walls. Surmounting each tower of the circlet are statues of the gods of the Cannorian Pantheon, encrusted with innumerable jewels. At the center, linked to the interior of the wall by bands of metal, lies an astonishingly accurate representation of Trialmount, topped with a huge diamond!

But that is not all, as there are actually two different parts in this masterpiece! Our smiths forged a splendid miniature dragon, and the most talented enchanter of our realm created an invisible magic link between the two parts, so that the dragon can levitate atop the crown! The mighty Silver Dragon of Castanor deploying its wings around Castan's head as he speaks is truly a sight to behold.

  • Maximum Absolutism: +15 (max_absolutism; raw value 15).

Castanorian Ambition

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

Castellyr (B31) — Castellyrian Ideas

Set ID: B31_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B31
    }

Castellyrian Traditions

  • Fort maintenance: -30% (fort_maintenance_modifier; raw value -0.3).

  • Diplomatic relations: +2 (diplomatic_upkeep; raw value 2).

1. Order of the Sapphire Eye

The Order of the Sapphire Eye was a pre-Greentide knightly order devoted to chivalric virtues and maintaining the peace in Escann, fighting in duels or tourneys known as the 'Trials of Chivalry' as a more peaceful alternative to settle disputes between the Escanni realms. With the rebirth of our kingdom, this order has returned from its near-annihilation to offer us their support in bringing peace back to Escann. Not only does this let our knights train under some of the greatest veterans of the Greentide, it also shows the world the virtue and validity of our claims!

  • Cavalry combat ability: +15% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.15).

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -10% (ae_impact; raw value -0.10).

2. True Heirs of Castan

After the War of the Sorcerer-King, Castanor was broken into disparate realms, some of the greatest of which were the Kingdom of Cast and the Kingdom of Anor. Eventually, these were united under one kingdom - Castellyr, the rightful successor to Castanor. We are the obvious inheritors of this legacy, having accomplished the same.

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

3. Bringers of Peace

Our ambition to bring peace once again to Escann are respected even by our enemies, and even more by our defeated enemies who are often surprised by being integrated as countrymen rather than subjugated as enemies. This makes recruiting local collaborators and solidifying our control over new lands much easier.

  • Diplomatic annexation cost: -20% (diplomatic_annexation_cost; raw value -0.20).

4. Return of the Escanni

Many of our fellow Escanni fled west as refugees during the Greentide and are now returning to those lands we have pacified. Many have also returned to those lands claimed by the adventurer kingdoms. This makes assimilating the adventurer much easier, as we can simply surround them with native neighbors and let basic socialization do the work.

  • Culture conversion cost: -20% (culture_conversion_cost; raw value -0.20).

5. Nobility and Honor

With the return of stable government to Escann, chivalry has made a comeback. Though not as idealistic as it was before the Greentide, our chivalric traditions are still enough to motivate our soldiers to act with honor and seek glory.

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

6. Tourneys of Castellyr

The restoration of old Escanni traditions has also seen the resurrection of tourneys, as well as the resolving of disputes between parties through them. Not only does this make escalating to direct conflict socially unacceptable among our nobles, it also provides excellent entertainment for our people and suitable intimidation for would-be rebels.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

7. Wealth of Escann

Escann was a rich land before the orcs invaded, and we shall make it rich again! We shall sponsor a program of national rejuvenation with the goal of restoring our cities to their former glory.

  • Development cost: -10% (development_cost; raw value -0.1).

Castellyrian Ambition

  • Yearly absolutism: +1 (yearly_absolutism; raw value 1).

Adenica (B58) — Adenner Ideas

Set ID: B58_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B58
    }

Adenner Traditions

  • Missionary strength: +3% (global_missionary_strength; raw value 0.03).

  • Cavalry combat ability: +33% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.33).

1. Birthplace of Chivalry

The Kingdom of Adenica was the birthplace of the common ideals of "knights" and chivalry. When Adenica fell during the Greentide, that shining beacon of honour and chivalry was lost. With Adenica reforged again, we will rise to meet the ideals of our forefather and shine once more. With righteous hearts, our knights will reclaim their former glory as they ride against injustice.

  • Cavalry flanking ability: +100% (cavalry_flanking; raw value 1).

  • Cavalry to infantry ratio: +20% (cav_to_inf_ratio; raw value 0.2).

2. Sons of Adean

Adean is the first-born son of Castellos, and the god of honour, justice and chivalry. When our kingdom was founded, and now refounded, our people embraced these ideals in their entirety. To this end, every man, woman, and child holds this pledge in their hearts: "We are the spear of Adean and all he stands for. No matter what evil we face, we shall not falter."

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

3. The Corinite Heresy

There is no doubt in our minds that Corin deserved her ascent to godhood for her valiant sacrifice ending the Greentide. Yet this attempted usurpation of the Regent Court shows that perhaps it was truly Agrados reborn, not Corin ascendant, that has declared war upon the gods. The Corinites do not pledge themselves to Corin and her beliefs, but to Agrados. This vile heresy and desecration of both Corin's name and the Regent Court as a whole cannot be tolerated. We must be the spear of Adean once more.

  • Cost of enforcing religion through war: -50% (enforce_religion_cost; raw value -0.5).

4. Born to Fight

When Castanor fell, Adenica fought for its sovereignty against the other successor states. It fought to the last as the Greentide brought ruin to Escann. Even when struck down, its spirit continued to fight. And, through fire, blood and steel, Adenica was reforged. Adenners have never feared fighting for what was right and they are ready and willing to continue that fight once more.

  • War exhaustion: -0.03 (war_exhaustion; raw value -0.03).

5. Land of Honor

In Adenica, we pride ourselves on our high standards of honourable conduct. It is a core element of our culture and society, second only to our faith. This high level of honour and respect has led to a vastly lower level of corruption, blackmail and abuse of power within our bureaucracy.

  • Yearly corruption: -0.1 (yearly_corruption; raw value -0.10).

6. Knight-Kings of Adenica

To rule in Adenica, you must prove yourself worthy of rule. To do this, one must obtain knighthood before ascending to the throne. This has been a long standing tradition within our kingdom, and has proven profoundly useful. Our Knight-Kings are known throughout the world for their chivalrous and honourable conduct, and are role models to many rulers and heir-apparents. This reputation has left us in good standing within the global community.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

7. Between the Titans

Our proximity to both the Empire of Anbennar and the reborn realms of Escann have provided us a unique opportunity. We are able to draw on the regulations and innovations of the Western Cannorians, and the military expertise from the Escanni realms. We can leverage this advantage to stay head of the curve, and ensure our ability to protect those in need.

  • Global institution spread: +20% (global_institution_spread; raw value 0.2).

Adenner Ambitions

  • True faith tolerance: +2 (tolerance_own; raw value 2).

Blademarches (B33) — Blademarcher Ideas

Set ID: B33_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B33
    }

Blademarcher Traditions

  • Army morale: +15% (land_morale; raw value 0.15).

  • Infantry combat ability: +10% (infantry_power; raw value 0.1).

1. Calindal, the Gleaming Blade

The Gleaming Blade was a greatsword used during the Dragonwake by Elecast Dragonsbane to slay the dragon Alos the Copper. While the blade is known for its sharp vorpal quality, it is most famous for the fact that, once drawn, it shines a light that is capable of blinding those who stare too close - this blinding nature of the blade has been used since time immemorial to determine the worthiness of the Blademarcher kings.

During the Decade of Masks it was discovered that the Gleaming Blade was none other than Calindal, a precursor spellblade named after and forged by the mythological elf-smith Calindal.

  • Leader land shock: +1 (leader_land_shock; raw value 1).

  • Monarch military skill: +1 (monarch_military_power; raw value 1).

2. Revive the Bladestewards

The Order of the Bladestewards was a monastic order dedicated to protecting (Calindal, the Gleaming Blade) and ensuring that only the worthy may wield it and rule the Blademarches. Most members of the Blade Stewards are volunteers taken in by the Order, whether it be of unfortunate circumstance or simply a warrior looking for a higher cause. However, a small number of the Blade Stewards are known as Blind Masters, who are comprised of individuals who fail the test of the Gleaming Blade.

  • Army tradition: +0.5 (army_tradition; raw value 0.5).

3. Legacy of the Dragonslayers

Elecast Dragonsbane, the founder of the kingdom, is the first ever-recorded dragonslayer in history. Our founder's renown is unmatched, and many respect our history and nation for it.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +100% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 1).

4. Blade-Priests

By integrating our religion with the coronation of the monarch, we can strengthen both the devotion of our people to the faith and to the monarch.

  • Papal influence: +2 (papal_influence; raw value 2).

  • Yearly Corinite Paragonhood decay: raw value 0.1 (unit unverified) (yearly_karma_decay; raw value 0.1).

  • Religious power modifier: +10% (church_power_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Legitimacy: +1 (legitimacy; raw value 1).

  • Devotion: +1 (devotion; raw value 1).

  • Republican tradition: +0.3 (republican_tradition; raw value 0.3).

  • Horde unity: +1 (horde_unity; raw value 1).

5. Rise of the Bladechosen Kings

Calindal is Blademarch and Blademarch is Calindal. Any who wield the Gleaming Blade is a worthy ruler by default, and without them: we are nothing.

  • Yearly absolutism: +0.5 (yearly_absolutism; raw value 0.5).

  • Maximum Absolutism: +10 (max_absolutism; raw value 10).

6. Bright Hussars and Their Blinding Charge

A famous poem by Lord Wooley during the Fifth Blackpowder War, which details the last charge of the Blademarcher cavalry against a legion of mechanical soldiers:

"the last of the bright hussars came, with burning hearts and gleaming blade, onwards to mechanim death: fusillade, come powder's end: none remained."

-Lord Wooley (1853)

  • Cavalry combat ability: +15% (cavalry_power; raw value 0.15).

7. Meritocracy at War and Peace Act

The Meritocracy at War and Peace Act was enacted in 1670 during the Witch-Kings Era which reformed the army and government as a whole, replacing all official positions to those of merit not feudal standing, gender or influence.

  • Female advisor chance: +50% (female_advisor_chance; raw value 0.5).

  • May recruit female generals: Allowed (may_recruit_female_generals; raw value yes).

  • global_manpower_modifier: +15% (global_manpower_modifier; raw value 0.15).

Blademarcher Ambition

  • Discipline: +5% (discipline; raw value 0.05).

Farraneán (B60) — Farranean Ideas

Set ID: B60_upgraded_ideas. Source: project-verified Mod script (public artifact omits local path and line offsets).

Applicability condition (source script):

    trigger = {
        tag = B60
        has_country_flag = farranean_greater_ibevar_flag
    }

Farrani Traditions

  • Global trade power: +15% (global_trade_power; raw value 0.15).

  • National tax modifier: +10% (global_tax_modifier; raw value 0.1).

  • Female advisor chance: +40% (female_advisor_chance; raw value 0.4).

  • May recruit female generals: Allowed (may_recruit_female_generals; raw value yes).

1. Grove of the Scoghtrín

The symbol of our kingdom and centerpiece of the royal courtyard, the Scoghtrín is a solid black tree grown from a Cursewood sapling first planted in Escin to represent the unity between the elves and men of the eastern Vale. The magics of the tree helped to lessen the effects of the curses that have long plagued this land, and allowed our kingdom to thrive where others have faltered. Though the original may have been destroyed in the Greentide, its legacy lives on in all of us as our banner flies once more over the cities of the Forlorn Vale.

  • National unrest: -2 (global_unrest; raw value -2).

2. Sword, Spell and Shot

We have unified the Vale and more beyond, by the union of Elvish Instruction, Human Ingenuity, Half-Elven diplomacy and all those others who have a place in Farranean, we have built an army that surpasses what came before. The old separate armies of Ibevar and Farranean had their own strengths, but now they have come together in one spirit and shall not let the years forsake what unity between us all has brought. Just as there is the unity of spirit, so too comes the unity of technique. Bladedancing, War Magic and the Thunder of Cannons roar as one great cacophony on the fields where battle is drawn when our enemies face the Farrani Army.

  • Shock damage: +10% (shock_damage; raw value 0.1).

  • Infantry combat ability: +15% (infantry_power; raw value 0.15).

3. Cursewood Lumber

The Cursewoods are a largely untapped source of quality lumber, the superstitions and happenings of the Vale allowing them to grow thick and rich, untouched by civilization. They've long supplied the timber required to build our cities and villages, and so long as we maintain them properly they will continue to do so as we rebuild and expand the kingdom.

  • Construction cost: -10% (build_cost; raw value -0.1).

  • Production efficiency: +5% (production_efficiency; raw value 0.05).

4. Farrani Caseán

The White Pestilence, and the undead hordes it brought, ravaged the young kingdom of Farraneán. To survive we constructed heavily fortified towns known as Caseán to house our people during attacks. When the dust settled and we were allowed to return to our homes, many of our people stayed within the walls of these Caseán, maintaining them in anticipation of future crises or war with Ibevar. It was due to them that many of our people were able to escape from the Greentide, their walls holding just long enough for them to flee to safer lands.

With our kingdom restored the Caseáns shall be repopulated as well, ready to defend us against whatever the gods decide to send our way.

  • Fort defense: +15% (defensiveness; raw value 0.15).

5. Aldresian Oaths

The Orda Aldresia once guarded the Vale and the Empire both against the encroachment of the Corvurian realm, and then when the Greentide came were one of the first refuges for those fleeing the destruction that was wrought upon the continent. Their time is now over, their authority sublimated to that of the Farrani Crown. But this is not a tragic circumstance, for they continue as an order within our realm and their temporal authority ends only because the old promise of Aldresia and the oaths all knight gave stands fulfilled. They have new oaths now, to the Monarchs of Farranean and to the people of the Vale and Escann where once they served the Empire of Anbennar at their own peril. They split on the issue of Escann, but now Escann has mended them in full with our boundless patience.

  • Diplomatic reputation: +200% (diplomatic_reputation; raw value 2).

  • Aggressive expansion impact: -10% (ae_impact; raw value -0.1).

6. Cogaulúis Ball

Many of Farraneán's founders came from Esmaria, and they brought with them traditions of revelry and festivities. The most anticipated celebration of the year is the annual Ball held on several dozen barges moored in the Cogaulúis river as it runs through Escin. Commoners celebrate and peddle trinkets along the riverbank while wealthy nobles, merchants, and visiting dignitaries party and converse on the vessels. 1. Alenic Ancestry

During the Dragonwake, the Marrodic tribe fled south alongside their Rohibonic and Wexonard brethren to escape the wrath of Godrac the Invader, but the Gawedi Warlord did not relent. But when the Three Tribes were caught at Bal Hyl, alongside allies of convenience in the Damerian garrison of the citadel, they made a last stand. The ensuing victory pushed the Gawedi forces back, and the Damerian offered them land as a reward, and while the Wexonards accepted, the great king Marr had different plans in mind. He directed his people east, through the Korbarid kingdom to the lands of Castanor, recently ruined by the fury of dragons. The Korbarids mocked his plan, but the king was unwavering, and to those who doubted, he said:

“A tree felled by lightning shan't be struck twice!”

This phrase became the embodiment of the Marrodic spirit: a people so bold they seek refuge from the storm within its own eye. Be it during catastrophes or in battle, the Marrodics are steadfast and unwavering, just as King Marr was.

2. The Hold of the Griffon King

Long ago, the hold of Ânumdihr was abandoned, severed from the Serpentspine as the tunnels were destroyed to hold off the monsters lurking in the deep. When the Marrodics reached the hold in 492, they found an empty ruin suitable for their people to settle and rebuild. So began a long reconstruction effort in which the Marrodics rebuilt the hold; this process cost an astronomical amount of gold, mostly to handsomely reward the dwarven artisans Ulric III ‘the Great’ hired to finish the project. It was an arduous process, but in 549 they managed to fully rebuild the first level, the royal court moving into it soon after. While most remained within the Vale to work mainly as farmers and shepherds, Ânumdihr grew into the city of the Marrvale.

Its halls and homes were adjusted for human size, its walls adorned with tapestries and engraving of Alenic make, and the forges produced vast quantities of longswords and chainmail. No longer was this Ânumdihr, this was Marrhold, and the Marrodics were the Lords of the Vale.

3. Griffon Riders of Cannor

Legend has it that as the Marrodics settled the Marrvale and its great, though dilapidated and abandoned Dwarven hold, they were set upon by terrifying winged creatures that would descend from the mountains. With many either dying or being wounded by these attacks, King Marr sent his son, Ulric, to face these monsters. It is said Prince Ulric climbed high into the Serpentspine Mountains, reaching the nest of the griffons at the top. There, he battled them for many hours, eventually vanquishing the threat to his people. Once he had, however, he chose to spare their eggs, taking many with him on his descent.

In time, these griffons would grow into mighty steeds granted to King Marr’s finest warriors, with Ulric as the first Griffon Rider atop his steed, ‘Thundersteed’. Over the centuries, the Griffon Knights would come to dominate Marrodic society, the position given only to the highest ranking nobles, with the breeding and rearing of the steeds being a highly protected and regulated affair.

While some call our reliance on them foolish, citing our rigid social structure and low number of these elite troops, there is a reason why even after the Dragonwake, even the mightiest lords of Cannor dread the sight of something moving in the skies.

Since then the practice has evolved many times, first as a purely military drill, then as a noble tournament, but it was only in 1386 where both practices were officially conjoined.

Two different jousts are hosted each year in different locations and times. One is the traditional course of training, occurring in winter deep within the mountains above Marrhold, with scant few onlookers having ever caught a glimpse of this event. This training is reputed to be most arduous, carried out in extreme wind and snow. The second is a grand summer festival held in Griffonsgate, open to any citizen of Marrhold, in which Griffon-Knights show off in magnificent parade attire with long white cloaks floating in the wind. This event is famed for being the only opportunity to see so many griffons in the same place and for the aerial choreographies of renowned Griffon-Knights.

If a fort were to fall, the enemy would be allowed deeper in the multi-layered fortification system and their supplies harassed using the secret passages; ultimately, a deathly trap would close behind the enemies as any fort taken would be retaken by the Marrodics, isolating the enemies in a sea of hostile forts and trapped passages. This formation of forts was nicknamed “The Death Ring of Marrvale” by an enemy general that had its army cut in two and decimated by the formation.

As such, the Marrhold was unbroken. None managed to reach it for centuries; neither Nichmer, Dookanson, and though Marrhold submitted to Camir, not even he tried to besiege the hold, a source of great pride for the Marrodics.

King Ulric XVII Marr could not bear to see what many believe to be Marrhold’s strength be relegated to a simple exotic pet; as such, he invested greatly in our local artificers, commissioning them to develop weapons enabling the Griffon-Knights to attack while remaining airborne, whatever the conditions. Known as the Griffon Bombardier Squadron, they quickly replaced the traditional Griffon-Knights. The Bombardier Squadron were devastatingly effective, but to be deployed properly, they had to be able to resupply with ammunition and not be completely exposed to incoming fire, for griffons remained vulnerable to shot and shell during both the dive and during the climb after.
